question: Chhath Pooja is mainly celebrated in which of these states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhath Pooja** is a major Hindu festival primarily celebrated in the state of **Bihar**, as well as in parts of Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Nepal.
 
• The festival is dedicated to worshipping the **Sun God (Surya)** and Chhathi Maiya (a manifestation of Goddess Usha).
 
• It is celebrated over a span of four days with significant rituals including **fasting, holy bathing, and offering arghya (water) to the Sun God**.
 
• The festival is known for its strict rituals and is observed with utmost devotion, especially on the banks of rivers and water bodies.
 
• Key locations for Chhath celebrations in Bihar include **Patna, Gaya, and Bhagalpur**, where millions gather to perform rituals by the Ganga River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Chhath Pooja:**

 
 
• It is one of the oldest known Hindu festivals dedicated to environmental harmony and solar energy.
 
• The rituals symbolize gratitude towards the Sun God, believed to sustain life on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Four-Day Ritual Breakdown:**
 
 
• **Day 1:** Nahai Khai – Devotees take a holy dip and prepare traditional food.
 
• **Day 2:** Kharna – Observers fast throughout the day and break it after sunset with a simple meal.
 
• **Day 3:** Sandhya Arghya – Devotees offer prayers to the setting sun.
 
• **Day 4:** Usha Arghya – Prayers are offered to the rising sun, followed by ending the fast.
 
 
 
• **Chhathi Maiya:**
 
 
• Chhathi Maiya is considered the consort of the Sun God and is worshipped for the welfare of family and children.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Importance:**
 
 
• The festival promotes environmental awareness by encouraging cleaning of water bodies and surrounding areas.
 
• Fasting and exposure to sunlight during Chhath are believed to detoxify the body and enhance immunity.
